passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: 8.5 Giving human labour its value across villages and regions

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: The darshan’s valuation of labour needs records: the pace of work in each activity, the time and means each product requires, the quantities different producers achieve under different conditions, and the remuneration producers actually receive (AA, pp. 66, 119, 145). Within a single village for a staple crop, such records can be kept by hand. Between villages, districts, and regions, and for industrial products assembled from many inputs across tiers, manual calculation breaks down, and the connected production and exchange-reserve agents of §8.3 do the heavy computational work.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: Across the tier network, the agents keep labour records for each kind of product and compute a common value of labour from the range of yields and paces across many villages, as the treatise does for wheat within one village, updating it as techniques and generational means change (AA, pp. 66, 118, 145). They compute the labour embodied in complex goods by tracing their inputs back through the chain of production across cottage, small, medium, and large industries, using the input–output methods described in §4.10, including the depreciation of tools, machines, and buildings, so that the past labour used up in each round of production is accounted for without charging interest. Across villages and regions with unequal soil fertility, rainfall, or mineral access, the agents model differences in yield caused by natural endowment (Ricardo 1817) separately from differences in human effort and skill, so that midpoint valuation does not quietly penalise less fertile villages or award resource rents to more fertile ones. During the transition they maintain both measures side by side, prices in currency and values in labour, so that the second and third stages of the treatise’s path, evaluating currency on the basis of labour and then exchanging on labour value alone, have verified figures at every step (AA, pp. 142–143). They show each producer what their labour established and what they received for it, show each village where value is being siphoned off between producer and consumer, and match local skill profiles to the production a village needs so the education committee can plan training (AA, p. 131).

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: The method of valuation remains a human decision. The village council decides how object values are evaluated and consolidated, and the production and exchange-reserve committees jointly determine the quantity, quality, and value of labour for the village (AA, pp. 67, 143). Inside the family, contributions are not weighed at all (AA, pp. 119–120). The agents supply measurement, input–output tracing, and counterfactual modelling; people decide what counts as a fair common value and how differences of skill and circumstance are honoured. Giving labour its true value is also more than computing an exchange ratio. It means recognising what labour establishes, nourishment, protection, and social participation, and through right use the orderliness of the whole (§§3.5–3.6). Records of what products actually fulfilled for the families who used them belong to the same account.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: 8.6 Keeping the cycle in balance and accelerating the transition

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: Within the framework of §§8.3–8.4, the agent network turns the village survey into a living operational model rather than a one-time paper census, and summarises it for families and part-time committees in plain language. At the village level, the committee agents keep the exchange-reserve’s accounts, track stock and its age, compare extraction with regeneration for each natural asset, project when a trend will cross a regenerative limit, and estimate from the land and water of a village or district how many families it can support with prosperity (AA, p. 92). When an early failure signal appears, the relevant agent flags it immediately and presents the causal trace that produced the flag. Where a rule has already been settled by the council, for example the proportion of a forest that may be cut in a year, the reordering of a store, or the routing of seasonal surplus between neighbouring villages, the agent executes the routine coordination and reports what it did.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: Across the ten tiers from village to world, agent-to-agent communication addresses the coordination problem that markets delegate to prices and interest rates and state socialism delegates to central planning ministries (§§4.9–4.10). By continuously aggregating family and village need assessments alongside regional production capacities and ecological constraints, higher-tier agents let a district or province see the real-time balance of production and need across its villages, plan which village supplies what another lacks, schedule multi-year investments in shared infrastructure across tiers without relying on an interest rate, and clear exchange between regions at labour value (AA, pp. 72, 115, 118; MVD, p. 268).

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: This agent infrastructure also lowers the barrier to transition from the current system. Today, any community attempting to move toward cyclical economics must operate inside a global market economy whose price signals, credit terms, and supply chains are coordinated by advanced algorithmic systems tuned for profit. An isolated village cooperative relying on manual ledgers or static spreadsheets faces high transaction costs in running dual accounting (currency and labour value), matching diverse household needs with local multi-occupation output, and coordinating with other transitioning communities. When each new family, cluster, and village is equipped with pre-configured agents that already speak the common protocol of the five committees and ten tiers, a transitioning community can immediately conduct internal need assessment, run dual-stage exchange-reserve clearing (AA, pp. 142–143), pool surpluses with other participating villages across distances, and reduce its dependence on speculative currency markets step by step.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: 8.7 Automation, participation, and knowledge as a common

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: The darshan’s criterion for technique (§3.10) applies to AI with special force. AI and automation can take over drudgery, extend skill, and reduce the time production requires, which is the generational gain the treatise expects from means rightly used (AA, p. 118). They can also concentrate capital, displace producers, and replace the working mindset with a managing one, the very drives the treatise and the public discourse identify as obstacles (AA, p. 107; JVD, p. 35). A cyclical economy deploys AI to raise the usefulness each person’s labour establishes and to free time for study, family life, and participation in self-governance, while keeping every person engaged in physical production according to capacity, receptivity, and ability (MVD, p. 265; AI study §1.8). The test of any deployment is whether it keeps producers producing and lets them see the value of their work, or turns them into passive consumers and clerks managed by others.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: Because research and dissemination are inseparable and the powers of jeevan cannot be stored in any reserve (AA, pp. 56–58), the knowledge an AI system carries, its models, weights, protocols, and records of agricultural and craft practice, belongs among the means each generation hands on to the next. The treatise already expects every committee from the village to the world to share information through a computer system (AA, p. 132). The Personal, Family, and Committee AI Agents built for a cyclical economy must therefore be open common infrastructure owned by the communities that use them, carrying technical knowledge to ordinary producers as teachers are asked to do (AA, p. 29) rather than being enclosed as proprietary intellectual property for rent or profit.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: 8.8 Governance, safeguards, and what must return to people

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: The questions in the last column of §8.4 are of a different kind from the calculations performed by the agent network. Whether a family’s assessment of need is true and fair, whether an exchange is free of exploitation, whether a member’s share in production matches ability and receptivity, whether a technique accords with orderliness, and whether a use of the forest serves the earth’s balance are questions of justice, dharma, and truth. The treatise assigns them to people and institutions: the family representative evaluates the members of the family, the family cluster evaluates its representative, the village council decides the method of valuing objects, and the justice-security committee resolves disputes through a reformative process (AA, pp. 67, 128–129, 139–140). At every level of the ten-tier architecture, an AI agent is paired with a human unit as an instrument (yantra), never as an autonomous authority: it ends its work by presenting the evidence, the trade-offs, and the question to the person, family, or committee responsible, not by deciding on their behalf.

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: Several architectural safeguards follow directly from the darshan’s account. First, no agent at any tier may be optimised for the perspectives that drive the open spiral, maximising throughput, engagement, attention capture, or monetary gain, since that would turn the infrastructure into an amplifier of the error described in §2 (AI study §1.5; Technical Note §1). Second, data custody follows the subsidiarity of the ten tiers: a person’s reflective logs belong to the person, a family’s internal records belong to the family, and village records remain open and accountable to the villagers (AA, p. 128), with higher-tier agents receiving only the aggregated balances needed for inter-tier coordination. Third, the agent network must not become a technocratic seat of rulership: power and centralised rule carry the direction of non-coexistence, and universal orderliness is participatory (AA, p. 82). Every model rule, labour-valuation formula, and ecological threshold used by the agents must remain inspectable and revisable by the councils they serve. Fourth, the material, mineral, and energy footprint of computing hardware and model training belongs within the cycle it serves, counted against regenerative limits like any other branch of production (AI study §1.7).

passages.heading: 8-bringing-the-economy-into-balance-measurement-intelligent-systems-and-multi-level-ai-agents
passages.section: 8. Bringing the economy into balance: measurement, intelligent systems, and multi-level AI agents
passages.text: The multi-level agent architecture described here applies the darshan’s distinctions to intelligent instruments that did not exist when the texts were written; the texts speak of computers as aids to exchange-reserve accounting and world-wide committee communication (AA, pp. 132, 138) and state the general rule for trusting instruments (KD, p. 139). Whether settled rules can be stated precisely enough for agents to apply them across ten tiers, whether diagnostic feedback helps anubhav-gami individuals and families overcome conditioned habits of overconsumption, how far computed labour values can be relied on across complex supply chains, and how communities can govern a federated agent network without ceding judgement to it are questions for practice, collected with the other open problems in §9.7. The companion technical note on a personal AI assistant sets out the criteria of source fidelity, non-manipulative design, and human benefit that every agent in this hierarchy would need to satisfy.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9. Critical review

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.1 Madhyasth Darshan — an explanation of insatiability with a demanding institutional path

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: It explains rather than postulates insatiability. The distinction between the body’s definite needs and jeevan’s need for continuity of happiness, together with the account of an inexhaustible selection-and-taste cycle without higher regulation, gives a mechanism for why want outruns need and why the satiation point recedes.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: It unifies diagnoses that other traditions hold separately: Aristotle’s and Marx’s account of limitless money-making, Polanyi’s account of disembedded markets, Keynes’s and Hirsch’s relative needs, the ecological account of throughput, and the Gita’s account of desire.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Its definition of wealth as produced objects and of capital as human labour power keeps economics tied to provision and makes the critique of symbolic value precise.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: By pairing need-based sharing inside the family with equal labour-value exchange between families, villages, and regions, it avoids both the market reduction of family life to exchange and the state-socialist deferral of need-based distribution to a distant historical stage.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Its cycle includes the renewal of human capacity and the closure of need, not only the closure of material loops, and it nests the economy within the balances of nature and the five dimensions of human orderliness.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: It offers a concrete institutional path, with surveys, an exchange-reserve, a staged transition from market prices to labour values, and evaluation criteria for each committee.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Its policy names the value of human labour explicitly: everyone engaged in production, honour according to capacity, prevention of the exploitation of the fruits of labour, and exchange at labour value within and between nations.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: It gives a clear rule for instruments: they embody human mentality, deserve bounded trust, and must have their signals read by people.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: The definiteness of need depends on awakening, which the darshan itself describes as not yet established in human tradition. The economic proposal therefore rests on a prior transformation whose spread has not been demonstrated at scale.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: The valuation of labour by pace, time, and means meets the problems classical and Marxian economics faced in reducing heterogeneous labour to a common measure, accounting for capital depreciation without an interest rate, and adjusting for Ricardian differential rent when natural fertility or mineral access varies across villages and regions. Midpoint averages may work for wheat within a village; their extension to complex, multi-stage products made across unevenly endowed regions needs the accounting methods discussed in §§4.2, 4.10, and 8.5, which the treatise does not itself develop.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Coordination beyond the village relies on part-time councils and committees linked by computers (AA, pp. 127, 132, 138). Passive databases and network connectivity alone cannot perform the real-time information processing and intertemporal allocation that prices and interest rates address (§§4.4, 4.9, 8.2); §§8.3 and 8.6 show why an infrastructure of multi-level AI agents paired with individuals, families, committees, and tiers is needed to supply that coordination without creating a full-time bureaucracy.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: The critique of specialisation (AA, pp. 70–71) sits uneasily with the special aspirations the darshan endorses, telephony, broadcasting, and transport, which depend on highly specialised production; the treatise’s own allowance for large industries at higher tiers suggests the objection is to specialisation severed from wholeness, but this is not made explicit.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Several of the treatise’s natural-science claims, on the earth’s magnetic current and on cosmic rays and water, go beyond present evidence and weaken its ecological argument where its general claims are well supported.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Madhyasth Darshan gives the most complete account of why human economies do not reach balance, and its institutional proposal is more specific than most alternatives, but its practicability depends on conditions it has yet to evidence beyond small communities.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.2 Neoclassical economics — coordination without a stopping point

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: It provides powerful tools for coordinating production and exchange among very large numbers of people who do not know one another.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Its methods of measurement, national accounts, input–output analysis, and the study of incentives, are indispensable to any economy that must assess its own condition.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Treating non-satiation as an assumption rather than a doctrine allows its models to be adapted.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: By taking wants as given, it has no account of why they grow and no criterion for when enough has been produced.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Its measure of success, growth of output valued in money, counts depletion of natural assets as income and rewards artificial scarcity.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Its separation of economics from the purposes of human life leaves those purposes to be supplied by whatever wants prevail.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Neoclassical economics coordinates without a stopping point, and its tools can serve a cyclical economy only if that economy supplies the criteria the discipline leaves out.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.3 Marxian and ecological economics — a sound diagnosis on a different ground

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Marx’s analysis of the circuit of capital and of the endlessness of accumulation in money matches the darshan’s critique closely.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Ecological economics grounds the limits of growth in thermodynamics and earth-system science and has developed measures of throughput and planetary boundaries.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Marx’s reliance on class conflict as the motor of change conflicts with the darshan’s account of complementarity and has produced coercive regimes in practice.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Ecological economics explains continued growth by institutions, debt, competition, and employment, without an account of the person whose wants those institutions serve, and so it struggles to make restraint chosen rather than imposed.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Marxian and ecological economics diagnose the open spiral soundly from the side of capital and of nature, and the darshan supplies the side of the person that both leave undeveloped.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.4 Gandhian economics — the closest relative

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Kumarappa’s economy of permanence and Schumacher’s Buddhist economics share the darshan’s village autonomy, cyclical agriculture and energy, production by the many, and restraint of wants.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: They have a long record of practical experiment in Indian villages and in appropriate-technology movements.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Their restraint of wants rests on moral and religious exhortation, simplicity as a virtue, rather than on an account of why wants become insatiable and how understanding makes them definite.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: They give little attention to the valuation of labour and to a staged transition from money exchange.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Gandhian economics is the nearest relative of cyclical economics in practice, and the darshan offers it a foundation in the understanding of jeevan that it lacks.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.5 Advaita and Indian ethics — a diagnosis of desire without an economic architecture

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: The Gita and Advaita give a penetrating account of desire as arising from mistaken identification with body and mind, and agree with the darshan that enjoyment does not quiet desire.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: The ordering of artha under dharma gives wealth a place without making it the aim of life.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Their remedy is directed inward, to knowledge of the Self and detachment, and offers no institutional design for production and exchange.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Treating the empirical world as of lower reality makes the economy a field to be transcended rather than an order to be established.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Advaita Vedanta and Indian ethics share the darshan’s diagnosis of desire, and the darshan differs in turning the remedy outward into family, production, and exchange.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.6 What the darshan can learn from economics

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Six lessons from economic theory bear directly on cyclical economics. First, coordination beyond the village needs active information processing, not only passive database connectivity, and the treatise’s own transitional reliance on market rates shows that prices carry knowledge which part-time councils will have to obtain through intelligent coordination infrastructure of the kind proposed in §§8.2–8.6. Second, prosperity and production security can be evidenced only if they are measured, and national accounting, input–output analysis, material-flow accounting, and life-cycle assessment provide methods for doing so. Third, Ostrom’s work on commons and Polanyi’s analysis of embeddedness show how institutions that govern shared natural assets and keep land, labour, and credit within social bounds can be designed and tested. Fourth, the theories of human need and capability of Max-Neef, Doyal and Gough, and Sen can sharpen the family’s assessment of need and guard it against both adaptive preference and paternalism. Fifth, an account of money as credit created through lending, together with the experience of mutual-credit clearing networks such as the Swiss WIR (BoE 2014; Stodder 2009), lets the darshan’s critique of symbolic value and its design for the exchange-reserve address present financial institutions directly. Sixth, input–output analysis, the debate over labour-time calculation, and classical rent theory show how the labour embodied in complex goods, capital depreciation, and differential natural fertility can be computed and separated (§§4.2, 4.10, 8.5).

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: 9.7 Open problems

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Several questions remain unsettled.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Need at scale. How does family-level assessment of need aggregate across a district or a nation, and how are disagreements between families’ assessments resolved without either imposing a standard or abandoning definiteness?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Labour valuation, depreciation, and differential rent. How should common values of labour be set and revised when skills, tools, capital depreciation, and natural endowments of soil, water, and minerals differ widely across regions, and how far can computed labour values for goods that pass through many hands and places be relied on (§§4.2, 4.10, 8.5)?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Coordination and long-term investment without prices or interest. What replaces the information carried by prices and the intertemporal rationing performed by interest rates in the third stage of the transition, and how much can a federated network of AI agents paired with committees across the ten tiers supply without creating a technocratic bottleneck (§§8.2–8.3, 8.6)?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Automation and participation. How can AI and other machines reduce drudgery and the time production takes without displacing people from production or concentrating control of the means (§8.7)?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Specialisation and the special aspirations. What division of labour is compatible with the darshan’s critique of specialisation, given that telephony, broadcasting, and transport require it?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Transition within a debt economy. How does an exchange-reserve working without interest coexist with banks that create money through interest-bearing loans, and what happens when the guarantor bank’s terms change?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Evidence. What observations in communities practising the darshan would show that needs become definite, that production exceeds need, that producers receive the value of their labour, and that material throughput falls? Systematic observations of this kind remain to be gathered.

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Natural-science claims. Which of the treatise’s claims about the earth’s balance, beyond the general dependence of production on natural regeneration, can be tested, and how should those not supported by present earth science be treated?

passages.heading: 9-critical-review
passages.text: Multi-level AI agents and human judgement. Can Personal, Family, and Committee AI Agents help anubhav-gami individuals and families overcome conditioned priya–hita–labha habits during the transition, and can communities govern a ten-tier agent network without ceding to it the judgements of justice, dharma, and truth or allowing it to be redirected toward profit (§§8.3, 8.8)?

passages.heading: 10-conclusion
passages.text: 10. Conclusion

passages.heading: 10-conclusion
passages.text: Human economies do not reach balance because the need they are asked to meet is not the need they can meet. The body’s requirements are definite, and the rest of nature shows what balance with them looks like. Jeevan seeks continuity of happiness, and in delusion it pursues that continuity through the transient satisfactions of selection and taste, reading each failure as a shortage of objects. Accumulation, especially of money, gives this pursuit an object that never decays and never satisfies, and an economy organised around it extracts from the earth without limit and calls its imbalance growth.

passages.heading: 10-conclusion
passages.text: Cyclical economics answers by closing the cycle at the points where it now runs open. Need is assessed and made definite within the family; labour applied to natural abundance produces objects for use; the objects nourish and protect the body and sustain social life, which renews the capacity to produce; labour is valued by the usefulness it establishes, and exchange follows that value, so that remuneration equals production and leaves no room for profit; production stays within the proportions of natural regeneration; and the remainder flows into right use. The economy is one dimension of a self-governing order of families and villages, and it cannot be separated from education, health, and justice.

passages.heading: 10-conclusion
passages.text: Economic theory has much to teach this proposal about coordination, measurement, commons, needs, money, and the calculation of labour values. Passive databases and network connectivity alone cannot establish or run such an order across ten tiers while keeping governance part-time and every citizen a producer, nor can they guide individuals and families through the transition while habits of delusion are still being examined. An infrastructure of intelligent systems and AI agents paired with each human unit, from the Personal AI Assistant and Family AI Agent to the committee and council agents across all ten tiers, can accelerate the transition and keep the conditions of the cycle visible and coordinated far faster than static ledgers alone. The darshan’s distinction between law, regulation, and balance on one side and justice, dharma, and truth on the other gives these agents a clear boundary. They can help bring the economy into balance by measuring, computing input–output labour values, warning of failure points, and coordinating across committees and tiers, while returning to people the questions of whether a need is real, an exchange just, a valuation fair, and a use consistent with the order of the whole. The economy the darshan describes depends finally on understanding, and no instrument can supply that. What well-governed agents can do is lower the cognitive and administrative barrier to transition and show quickly and plainly where understanding is still needed.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Appendix: Quick Glossary

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Cyclical economics (avartansheel arthshastra): the right use, security, and prosperity of resources in the form of body, mind, and wealth, organised as a cycle that returns to its starting point with its purpose fulfilled. The working economy is the cyclical economy (avartansheel arthvyavastha).

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Cyclicality (avartansheelta): complementarity and mutual sustenance, a movement that passes through complementary activity towards a goal and returns to its starting point.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Resources (artha): body, mind, and wealth together (where “mind” denotes the jeevan powers as a whole, distinct from the specific faculty mun).

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Wealth (dhan): produced objects carrying usefulness value and aesthetic value; not money.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Natural abundance (prakritik aishvarya): earth, air, water, forest, and minerals, the sites where labour is utilised.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Value (mulya): a unit’s participation in the orderliness of the whole; for produced things, their usefulness and aesthetic value.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Value of labour (shram mulya): the value of human labour, judged by the usefulness and aesthetic value it establishes; the basis on which produced objects are valued and exchanged. Valuing labour is the act of evaluating that usefulness and aesthetic value through the labour that established them.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Common aspirations and special aspirations (samanya akanksha, mahatvakanksha): food, shelter, and adornment (together with objects for health and education); telephony, broadcasting, and transport.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Production in excess of need (avashyakta se adhik utpadan): the condition of prosperity in every family.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Wise family (samajhdar parivar): a family endowed with understanding, in which two to four members may produce beyond the family’s whole necessity.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Prosperity (samriddhi): the absence of the sentiment of lacking; production in excess of need, with its right use and security.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Social participation (samaj gati): the contribution and movement of a person and family towards society and orderliness; paired with the nourishment and protection of the body as the domain in which produced objects are useful.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Use, right use, and purposeful use (upyog, sadupyog, prayojansheelta): utilisation of body, mind, and wealth in the nourishment and protection of the body and social participation; in orderliness and undivided society; and in evidencing understanding from generation to generation.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Exchange-reserve (vinimay kosh): the village institution through which produced objects are exchanged without profit and loss.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Righteous wealth (svadhan): wealth received as remuneration of one’s own labour, as a gift, or as an award; its opposite is ill-gotten wealth, obtained through exploitation and hypocrisy.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Generosity (udarta): the happy offering of body, mind, and wealth, according to need, for the awakening, health, and prosperity of others.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Three motives (putreshana, vitteshana, lokeshana): the humane propensities for progeny, wealth, and public welfare or reputation.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Three policies (dharm-neeti, arth-neeti, raj-neeti): moral policy (the right use of resources), economic policy (production beyond the family’s needs), and state policy (the protection of resources).

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Accumulation (sangrah): gathering beyond use; hoarding where it exceeds need.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Profit-obsession (labhonmad): the pursuit of giving less and taking more without a satiation point.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Symbolic currency (prateek mudra): metal or paper currency standing for objects; its value is symbolic value.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Satiation point (tripti bindu): the point at which an activity is fulfilled; accumulation, comfort, and profit have none.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Autonomous human (swayatt manav): a person who trusts in oneself, respects excellence, is balanced in talent and personality, social in behaviour, and self-reliant in occupation.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Authority, identity, and independence (adhikar, swatva, swatantrata): the strength of understanding and realisation, evidencing that strength in living, and unconstrained participation in family and universal orderliness.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Balance (santulan): the definite, mutually sustaining condition that each order maintains in its existent state; for the human order it is evidenced as resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Law, regulation, and balance (niyam, niyantran, santulan): the orderliness evident in nature, which humans understand and maintain.

passages.heading: appendix-quick-glossary
passages.text: Justice, dharma, and truth (nyaya, dharma, satya): the human evaluations of relationship, of participation in universal orderliness, and of coexistence.

passages.text: Source status of Avartansheel Arthshastra

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Avartansheel Arthshastra (AA) is cited from the project’s working English translation of the 2024 printing, a complete first pass now under the author’s review. AA and the Karm Darshan working translation (KD) are paraphrased with page citations; the block quotations come from Rakesh Gupta’s published translation of Jeevan Vidya. Janvad (JVD) and Adhyatmvad (AVD) are cited from Sanjeev Chopra’s translations in progress. AA, KD, MVD, and JV are cited by printed page (in KD, pp. 4, 7, 14, and 15 refer to the separately paginated introductory front matter), and SB, JVD, and AVD by page in the project’s PDFs. Passages of AA whose Hindi structure is unclear are indexed in the translation workspace; where the argument depends on one, the reading adopted is recorded in the notes below.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The definition of cyclicality

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The treatise’s definition of cyclicality (AA, p. 15) is flagged as unclear in the translation workspace (U-011). Its central phrase is an unpunctuated compound of natural abundance, naturalness, and natural complementarity, and it is not certain what is “linked”: resources, the process, or the points of the cycle. §3.2 adopts the reading that a cycle starts from any point, passes through complementary activity in the sense of prosperity towards the fulfilment of a goal, and returns to its starting point. This reading is supported by the examples on the same page, by the identification of cyclicality with complementarity and mutual sustenance (AA, p. 42), and by the provision sequence (AA, p. 106). The study’s argument does not depend on choosing among the parsings.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The provision cycle and replenishment

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The project’s introductory primer presents avartansheel as cyclical or replenishing production, attending to what is taken from nature and returned. The Jeevan Vidya lectures define the cycle as the renewal of human capacity through production, nourishment, and social participation (JV, p. 154). The treatise supports both and relates them. The provision cycle is the definition (AA, pp. 26, 106), and the use of natural assets in proportion to their production, without obstructing and while helping their production, is its condition (AA, pp. 114, 142, 146). §3.3 and §3.8 present them in that relation.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Cyclicality and natural recurrence

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The Karm Darshan working translation renders sahajavritti and anukshan-vikshan-vritti as “natural recurrence”. These terms concern the continuity of contemplation in jeevan, not economic or natural cyclicality, and are not used in this study.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The synthesis on insatiability

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: §2.3’s claim that insatiability arises from pursuing a continuous need of jeevan through transient means is assembled from connected passages: the four and a half effective activities and the internal conflict of the rest (JV, pp. 72–73), the absence of universal agreement in body-rooted deliberation by pleasure, health, and profit versus the universal agreement of justice, dharma, and truth in coexistence (AA, pp. 18–20, 58–60; MVD, p. 203), the inexhaustibility of selection and taste (AA, pp. 17–18), the transience of sensory satisfaction (JV, pp. 162–163; AA, p. 48), the indefiniteness of needs pursued as indulgence (MVD, p. 128), and the regulation of taste by the higher faculties in awakening (AA, p. 95). No single passage states the whole claim, and its phrasing as a “category error” is this study’s.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Pairings of use with justice, resolution, and authenticity

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The treatise pairs usefulness with justice, right use with resolution, and purposeful use with authenticity (AA, p. 116). A later passage describes usefulness as the exposition of the primacy of justice, dharma, and truth “in sequence” (AA, p. 118), which is flagged as unclear (U-129) and may have lost the other two terms of the triad. §3.5 follows the clearer passage.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Specialisation

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The treatise criticises specialisation for losing sight of wholeness, citing pest control and fertiliser that damage the agriculture they were meant to serve (AA, pp. 70–71), and criticises specialists who demand much while producing little (JV, p. 153). It also endorses telephony, broadcasting, and transport as special aspirations and provides for large industries at the higher tiers of self-governance (AA, pp. 29–30, 115). The study reads the criticism as directed at specialisation severed from wholeness and from production, and records the tension in §9.1 and §9.7.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Market rates in the transition

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: In the first stage of exchange, the exchange-reserve values local produce at the nearby wholesale rate less transport (AA, pp. 136–137, 142). This is a transitional use of prices, not a departure from valuation by labour, which the treatise reaches in the third stage. §9.6 reads it also as evidence that prices carry information which a labour-based system will need to obtain in another way.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Artificial intelligence and the multi-level agent architecture

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The primary texts do not discuss artificial intelligence. They speak of computers in the village exchange-reserve (AA, p. 138) and of a computer system linking committees from the village to the world so that information located anywhere is available to the village (AA, p. 132), and they state the general rule for trusting instruments (KD, p. 139) and the criterion for technique (AA, pp. 107, 118; SB, p. 267). §8 analyses why passive databases and network connectivity alone cannot satisfy the staffing, calculation, translation, and transitional demands of the treatise’s institutional design, and extends the placement of AI in the material order and the personal-assistant architecture developed in Artificial Intelligence and Coexistence and its technical note on a personal AI assistant into a multi-level agent architecture paired with individuals, families, the five committees, and all ten tiers of self-governance. Both the critique of passive database infrastructure and the multi-level agent proposal are this study’s extension, governed by the darshan’s distinction between law, regulation, and balance and justice, dharma, and truth (MVD, p. 173; AA, pp. 18, 117).

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Terminology

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Santulan is rendered as balance throughout, following MVD’s account of each order as balanced in its existent state (MVD, p. 105). “Stability” was considered for the study’s question but would suggest mere persistence, whereas santulan names a mutually sustaining relation with the rest of nature. The English renderings of AA’s economic vocabulary follow the decisions approved for the translation and adopted project-wide in October 2026: cyclical economics and cyclical economy for avartansheel arthshastra and arthvyavastha, cyclicality for avartansheelta, value of labour for shram mulya, production in excess of need for avashyakta se adhik utpadan, satiation point for tripti bindu, exchange-reserve for vinimay kosh, social participation for samaj gati, wise family for samajhdar parivar, and food, shelter, and adornment for ahar, avas, alankar. Where the published JV translation uses “clothing” for alankar in a quotation, the quotation keeps its wording.
